# Chapter 19 — Customer Module QRs (Merchant Portal "Printed QR")

> The Customer Module lets a merchant create **static, reusable, customer-specific KHQR codes** in the PayWay Merchant Portal — one QR per entity (a student, a vending machine, a distributor, a donation point). Customers pay any amount, any time, from any KHQR-compatible banking app. There is **no QR-generation API**: integration effort concentrates entirely on the **callback handler** and the **`get-transactions-by-mc-ref` reconciliation fallback**, both of which this SDK ships first-class support for.

**Sources of truth:** this chapter folds two merchant-captured knowledge bases
(`docs/archive/customermoudle-guide.md`, `docs/archive/customer module.md`) into
the SDK surface. Sample bodies and payload decodes below are REAL captured data
(portal customer `dhitraj`, outlet "Donation outlet", Customer ID
`dt-one-8989`, 2026-08-18) — pinned by tests in
`src/__tests__/customer-callback.test.ts`.

---

## 1. What it is (and what it is NOT)

| Aspect | Customer Module QR | Online QR (`generate-qr`) | Offline QR (`--offline`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generated by | Merchant Portal (only) | QR API | Your own code (SDK EMVCo builder) |
| Type | Static, per-customer | Dynamic, transaction-specific | Static, self-managed |
| Amount | Open (payer enters) or fixed | Fixed in payload | Fixed in payload |
| Reuse | Unlimited, no expiry | Single-use | Multi-use |
| Customer attribution | Server-side (PayWay routing tags) | n/a | None |
| Callback | **HMAC-signed** payment notification | HMAC-signed callback | Unsigned notification (no published auth contract) |
| Reconciliation API | `get-transactions-by-mc-ref` (Customer ID = `merchant_ref`) | check-transaction/detail | None (self-managed) |

Portal prerequisites (ABA-side, no code can replace them):

1. **Invoicing Tool or Payment Links must be enabled** on the merchant profile — the Customers module is otherwise hidden.
2. **Customer ID must be a mandatory, unique field** in the portal's Customize Fields settings (duplicate validation runs on mandatory fields only). This is the golden key: PayWay attributes every payment on that QR to the customer record and returns the Customer ID as `merchant_ref` in the callback and the reconciliation API. Keep it ≤ 20 ASCII characters (the inquiry gateway cap).
3. **QR-scoped API keys** must be requested from the integration team for the "Fetch Transaction Details by QR" endpoints (distinct from general merchant keys).
4. QR generation itself is portal-only (single, or batch ZIP for up to 100 customers at a time). There is no API to create customers or generate these QRs — batch Excel upload (≤1,000 rows, 5 MB) is the only programmatic customer path.

Operational warnings worth knowing before print:

- **Disabling override settlement BLOCKS existing customer QRs** (payments revert to the default account and downloads disappear). Override accounts must share the merchant's CIF; override accepts ABA Pay/KHQR only.
- A customer who has paid at least once **cannot be deleted** — reconciliation by Customer ID is permanent.
- Regenerating a QR changes the embedded `99.00` merchant-profile ID while keeping the same bakong account — retire old prints after regeneration.
- Vouchers do not apply to Printed QR payments.

---

## 2. Callback contract (verified against a real capture)

The payment notification POSTs to the merchant profile's **single configured callback URL** (configured by the ABA integration team against your Merchant Profile ID; changes in production require a formal support ticket). Expect:

- **Body:** KHQR-notification fields (`transaction_id`, `payment_status`, `payment_status_code`, `original_amount/currency`, `payment_amount/currency`, `payment_type`, `transaction_date`, `bank_ref`, `apv`, `payer_account`, `payer_name`, `bank_name`, `merchant_ref`) **plus a nested `customer` object** (`type`, `customer_id`, `customer_name`, `vat_tin`, `email`, `phone`, `address`, `remark`) and optional portal custom fields.
- **Signature:** `X-PAYWAY-HMAC-SHA512` header (HMAC-SHA512, Base64) — same scheme as the online checkout contract, so `payway.verifyCallback()` applies. The one captured sample's canonicalization matches the SDK verifier.
- **Money:** `original_amount/original_currency` is the merchant-side obligation; `payment_amount/payment_currency` is the payer's debit and may differ (currency or FX). Match obligations against `original_*`, never `payment_amount`.
- **Timing:** respond HTTP 200 within 5 seconds; **ABA does not retry** — a missed callback is recovered only by the reconciliation fallback (§4).
- **The Customer ID is NOT in the QR payload.** PayWay binds the QR to the customer record server-side (proprietary routing tags `62·68` + `99`); your join key is `merchant_ref` in the callback and API.

Real captured sample (also the fixture body):

```json

  "bank_ref": "100SB1787029448",
```

### 2.1 SDK surface

```ts
import { classifyCallback, parseCustomerQrCallback } from 'aba-payway-ts';

const kind = classifyCallback(parsedBody);
// 'online-checkout' | 'customer-module-qr' | 'khqr-offline' | 'payment-link-pushback' | 'unknown'

const parsed = parseCustomerQrCallback(parsedBody);
parsed.kind;                              // 'customer-module-qr'
parsed.notification.merchantRef;          // 'dt-one-8989' — the join key
parsed.notification.customer;             // portal profile snapshot
parsed.unknownFields;                     // forward-compatible catch-all
```

The parser never authenticates anything — parse, then **verify the signature**, then check state + money + dedupe before fulfilling (see the [Customer Module QR skill](../skills/aba-payway-customer-qr/SKILL.md) for the full outbox/idempotency handler).

### 2.2 Receiving with the SDK webhook server

`payway-sdk setup-webhook` hosts a capture server whose routes classify bodies, so one URL can serve every channel:

- `/aba-payway-khqr-webhook` is a development capture receiver for unsigned offline KHQR and signed Customer Module deliveries; it records header-based verdicts and metadata (`signatureVerdict`, `customerQr`, `matchedTransactionId/matchedStatus`, replay flag). Production merchant processing must select the enrolled service/profile/version contract in configuration, not downgrade a signed callback when its header is absent. Use separate routes/policies where needed and authoritative inquiry before posting.
- `/aba-payway-webhook` (the online route) classifies too — if your single profile URL points there, a Customer Module delivery still gets verified and tagged.
- `webhook list` shows `route=customer-qr customer_id=dt-one-8989` for such captures; `webhook verify-callback --record wh_…` re-reports the stored verdict.

Test the whole path without the Simulator:

```sh
payway-sdk webhook trigger --url http://localhost:8443/aba-payway-khqr-webhook \
  --event customer-qr.payment --merchant-ref dt-one-8989 \
  --amount 0.38 --customer-name dhitraj
```

## 3. QR payload anatomy (decoded from a real portal QR)

203-char KHQR/EMVCo TLV, decoded by `skills/aba-payway-customer-qr/scripts/decode-khqr.cjs`:

| Tag | Value | Meaning |
|------|--------------------------|---------|
| `01` | `11` | **Static QR** — reusable, no expiry (`12` = dynamic) |
| `30` | bakong ID + account + bank | KHQR Bakong merchant account template |
| `53` | `840` | Default currency USD (payer can switch if dual-currency) |
| `54` | *(absent)* | **No fixed amount** — payer enters it in-app |
| `62·68` | `PAYWAY@ABA`, outlet, merchant ID, flag | PayWay routing template (proprietary) |
| `99` | merchant profile ID, `mmp` marker | PayWay root extension (proprietary) |
| `63` | CRC-16 | Integrity checksum — never hand-edit; re-download from the portal |

**No Customer ID tag exists anywhere in the payload** — server-side attribution only.

## 4. Reconciliation fallback (`get-transactions-by-mc-ref`)

Because ABA never retries callbacks, every Customer Module integration needs a scheduled fallback job (every 5–10 minutes) that queries by Customer ID:

```ts
const result = await payway.khqr.getTransactionsByMerchantRef('dt-one-8989');
result.success;                 // statusCode '00'/'0'
result.rows;                    // normalized MerchantRefTransaction[]
result.rows.length >= 50;       // SATURATION — history may be truncated
result.raw;                     // untouched gateway envelope (audit)
```

Contract facts (merchant-captured; the sandbox KHQR domain 404s — Q36):

- **At most 50 rows, NO pagination.** A saturated (50-row) response is NOT a complete-history guarantee — treat it as a possible gap and cross-check against your own records.
- **Rate limit 10 requests/60 s** (enforced in the SDK client defaults).
- The merchant reference cap is 20 characters gateway-side.
- Envelope tolerance: production answers `{data: [...], status: {code: "00", …}}` while the doc page models `{status: number, transactions: []}` — the SDK normalizes both (`Q34`).
- Idempotency: dedupe on `transaction_id`; repeat payments on the same QR are legitimate separate transactions sharing one `merchant_ref`.

CLI:

```sh
payway-sdk get-transactions-by-ref --merchant-ref dt-one-8989
# prints the normalized result + raw envelope; warns on a 50-row page
```

Cron-ready script (durable checkpoint, dedupe, CSV, watch mode, GAP warning):

```sh
node skills/aba-payway-transaction-by-merchant-ref/scripts/reconcile.cjs \
  --merchant-ref dt-one-8989 --watch --interval 300 --csv payments.csv
```

## 5. Deployment checklist (Customer Module rows)

- [ ] Invoicing Tool / Payment Links enabled on the merchant profile (unlocks Customers module).
- [ ] Customer ID configured mandatory + unique in the portal; ≤ 20 chars; used as `merchant_ref`.
- [ ] One stable, public HTTPS callback URL handed to the ABA integration team (support ticket for production changes; **do not** provision an ephemeral `trycloudflare` URL — tunnels are for sandbox verification only).
- [ ] Callback handler: verify `X-PAYWAY-HMAC-SHA512` → require APPROVED → match `original_amount/original_currency` against the obligation → claim by `transaction_id` (unique constraint) → respond 200 within 5 s.
- [ ] Reconciliation cron via `get-transactions-by-mc-ref` with 50-row-saturation handling and `transaction_id` dedupe.
- [ ] QR-scoped API keys requested for the by-QR detail endpoints.
- [ ] Verbose callback logging (headers + raw body + computed hash) retained ≥ 30 days.
- [ ] Override-settlement decisions documented per customer (disabling blocks live QRs).
